title: Reinforcement-guided meta-threshold optimizer for canary rollback policies
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Goal: Build a meta-threshold optimizer that automatically suggests and applies rollback thresholds for canary/A-B/shadow deployments across multiple SLO signals (p95 latency, error rate, token cost per request, throughput). Approach: train an offline reinforcement learning (RL) policy over simulated rollout traces to recommend threshold vectors and hysteresis policies per cohort; during live canaries the policy runs in advisory mode and produces candidate thresholds plus uncertainty estimates. If modelled confidence is high and recommended thresholds are stricter than current conservative defaults, the rollout controller may apply them subject to conservative safety checks. Key ideas: 1) Use offline RL (batch-constrained) on historical canary traces + synthetic perturbations (traffic spikes, model quality regressions, noisy metrics) to learn risk-aware policies. 2) Represent state using a compact feature set: recent metric windows (latency quantiles, error counts), token cost delta, throughput, cohort metadata (region, model size), and time-of-day. 3) Learn a value function that estimates expected regret of allowing the rollout to progress vs triggering rollback; decision combines expected cost of false positive rollback vs expected customer impact of delayed rollback. 4) Use Thompson-sampling / Bayesian posterior on policy outputs for uncertainty; fall back to conservative threshold when uncertainty is high. 5) Integrate with rollout controller via a well-defined advisory API: (recommended_thresholds, confidence_score, reason_tokens). Success criteria: (a) reduce time-to-rollback for true regressions by >= 30% in staged canaries in internal canary-sim tests; (b) false-positive rollback rate remains <= current system's baseline; (c) enable cost-aware tradeoffs (e.g., prefer model-swap to rollback when token-cost increases but latency unaffected). Non-goals: fully autonomous online RL updates without human oversight in first phase. Rollout plan: Phase 0: offline data collection and sim harness (2 weeks). Phase 1: offline RL training + backtest against last 18 months of canaries (3 weeks). Phase 2: advisory-only shadow deployment for 2 weeks (compare decisions vs baseline). Phase 3: gated autopilot with manual approval and rapid abort capability (4 weeks). Observability: add per-decision telemetry in Console (decision rationale, input features, expected regret, alternate thresholds tested) and alert on decision drift. Safety: whenever confidence_score < 0.7 or the decision would reduce thresholds below a conservative floor, the controller must block and escalate to on-call. Implementation notes: use existing rollout simulator (see dependencies), store policies as versioned artifacts in model-catalog for auditability, and add replay recording for every canary to enable offline re-training. Privacy/security: all training uses aggregated/metric-level traces (no PII).
comments: 2026-03-02 — Initial scoping meeting: decided to prioritize offline RL + simulation rather than trying online bandits immediately. Marcus/CML provided initial data exports (canary-trace-2024.*).

2026-03-04 — Architecture review with infra and runtime teams. Trade-offs discussed: (1) model complexity vs explainability; we will surface simple 'reason_tokens' (e.g., 'latency_p95_spike_>20%') alongside numeric outputs. (2) Decision authority: advisory-only for Phase 2. Action: create advisory API spec (PRD link in attachments).

2026-03-06 — Design feedback from Lena Schultz (PM): include cost-accounting signal to prefer throttling/burst-limit adjustments before full rollback for token-cost regressions. Added as acceptance criteria.

2026-03-08 — Prototype training run completed on sim harness: offline policy reduces detection delay by ~28% on synthetic regression scenarios, but produced higher FP on low-traffic cohorts. Decision: add cohort-aware minimum-sample thresholds and confidence floor.

2026-03-10 — Security review flagged requirement to attach policy version + decision rationale to audit log. Security requests integration with KMS-signed policy manifests. Assigned to ENG-ops to advise.

2026-03-12 — PR draft opened for the advisory API and telemetry schema (https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-controller/pull/421). Seeking reviewers: @lena-schultz, @ryan-gupta (runtime), @devops-team. Next: run two-week shadow against production canaries starting 2026-03-20.
